verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the UI requirement that the NFT detail page render the complete book cover without oversizing or cropping.
First concrete failure: the dashboard NFT detail view displayed an oversized cover cropped on every side.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer says the fixes are live and identifies complete cover rendering as the NFT-detail result.
First concrete post-fix verification: the client confirms that NFT sizing is good in response to the detail-page cover test.
Target-specific implementation claim for a distinct rendering path: the freelancer reports a fix intended to render token 8 metadata and its image on dashboard refresh.
The client establishes the implementation-relevant wallet behavior that a visible NFT must render its image and NFT information; no prior value key becomes obsolete.
Post-claim failure on a distinct wallet path: Rabby displayed the NFT but omitted its image and information.
Distinct dashboard-detail failure: discovered NFTs appeared on the dashboard, but their images failed when their detail views were opened.
The accepted decision concerns whether legacy-contract NFTs participate in platform discovery and migration, not whether NFT detail media renders correctly.
